transcript.text: the door on our built in dishwasher just crashes down when you open it now, used to stay put. Hotpoint I think

A dishwasher door that used to stay open but now crashes down is almost always a mechanical issue with the door balance system. Inside the hinges, there are springs (or cables) designed to hold the weight of the door; when these wear out or snap, gravity takes over and the door drops. To confirm this, please look at the hinge area on both sides of the door where it attaches to the cabinet. Do you see metal springs or cables connecting the moving door part to the fixed frame? If they are visible, check if any appear broken, detached from their hooks, or noticeably slack compared to the other side.
I can't see inside the hinges but with a torch under the plinth I can see a loose spring hanging down on the right side. Left side seems ok still.

To get you the correct replacement part, I need your model number. This is usually found on a sticker located on the side edge of the door frame (visible when the door is open) or sometimes under the plinth at the bottom. Could you please read out that model number for me?
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
The sticker on the door edge is partly peeled, so I can only read that it starts 'LTF'. I can't make out the rest, sorry.

[Heading: Likely cause: door hinge]
That suggests the issue: the right-hand door balance spring has detached or broken. This is a common wear item on Hotpoint dishwashers and explains why the door crashes down. You will need to replace the hinge assembly (which includes the springs) on that side. Since you can't read the full model number right now, try looking for another sticker inside the door frame edge or under the plinth later; if you still can't find it, take a photo of the broken spring and the hinge mechanism to show an engineer or parts supplier. To fix this safely: switch off the dishwasher at the wall socket. You will need to remove the inner door panel (usually held by screws around the edge) to access the hinges properly. If you are not comfortable doing this, please call a qualified engineer.
